scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Parayan Thullal is one of the three major Thullal forms that emerged in Kerala, India.
It is part of a tradition of poetic performance that blends dance and storytelling.

Historically, these forms are linked to the cultural landscape of Kerala, specifically associated with figures like Mani Madhava Chakyar and institutions like Kerala Kalamandalam which have preserved the classical arts of the region.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Parayan Thullal is typically performed in the morning.
Unlike other Thullal forms that may focus on social satire, the stories in Parayan Thullal usually deal with spiritual matters and religious epics.
It serves as a medium for religious education and spiritual reflection through the arts.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The performance is characterized by a very slow tempo.
The dancer remains largely in an erect standing position with minimal footwork or complex dance sequences.
The primary focus is on the use of gestures to explain the literal and metaphorical meanings of the poetic verses being sung.
Watch for Erect Narrative Stance.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music of Parayan Thullal is defined by the use of the Sanskrit metre known as Mallika.
This metre dictates the slow, rhythmic delivery of the performance.
The pulse is Mallika metre.
A slow-paced vocal recitation of Sanskrit-influenced poetry, where the rhythm is governed by the Mallika metre, creating a steady and meditative atmosphere.

scenes.title: The people
narration: The tradition is associated with the broader history of Kerala's performing arts, which includes masters like Mani Madhava Chakyar and the pedagogical influence of the Kerala Kalamandalam institution.
Parayan Thullal is itself a variant within the Thullal tradition, distinct from Ottan Thullal (the most popular and fastest) and Sheethankan Thullal (medium tempo).
The dance is a subclass of Kerala dance and is categorized as a type of dance-drama and poetic performance form native to India.
